newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra changes affirmative action rules.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra changes affirmative action rules.

text.p: Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Tuesday the agency for the promotion of women in the workplace would soon change reporting requirements affecting Australian businesses.
"As from next year, those organisations that have achieved successful affirmative action programmes will no longer be required to submit reports to the agency every year," Reith said in a statement.
"This will help reduce unnecessary paper work for many businesses, while enabling a more positive focus for the Affirmative Action Agency."
Reith said the agency would establish a voluntary accreditation scheme, allowing businesses with high quality employment opportunity programmes for women to receive public recognition.
"More Australian businesses are now recognising the contribution of women to the workplace," he said.
"This year has seen an increase in the number of organisations with good affirmative action programmes."
Reith said the agency's focus increasingly would be on assisting businesses to put in place effective affirmative action programmes, rather than on sanctions.
